summary: ALPN downgrade + half-open socket accumulation causing elevated 5xx and streaming failures
description:
Issue summary:
A sustained elevation in 5xx responses (502/503/504) and streaming disconnects was observed for the ClaraDocs dedicated tenant beginning 2026-03-13 18:12 UTC. The spike affected a narrow set of routes handled by a subset of edge hosts and coincided with a high rate of short-lived streaming sessions from a third-party SDK that attempted TLS session reuse and sometimes fell back to HTTP/1.1.

Impact:
- ClaraDocs saw ~7-12% of requests failing with 5xx over a ~40 minute window.
- Streaming p95 latency increased to ~3.2s and several sessions experienced abrupt resets.
- A few serving-runtime pods reported worker thread starvation warnings and transient allocation failures followed by graceful restarts.

Environment:
- Production, us-east-1, ClaraDocs dedicated GPU pool.
- Edge: envoy v1.24 (custom build) accepting both HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 via ALPN.
- Serving runtime: redwood-runtime-2.7 on G5 instances.

Reproduction notes (partial):
1) Run a client that reuses TLS sessions and force fallback to HTTP/1.1 on reconnect.
2) Create short streaming sessions (~1-5s) at ~150 RPS scoped to a single tenant.
3) Watch envoy accept queue and socket TIME_WAIT / CLOSE_WAIT counts climb and PROTOCOL_ERROR resets appear.

Logs / Observations:
- Accept queue depth for several edge hosts rose from <5 to ~300+ concurrently.
- Kernel socket states showed elevated TIME_WAIT and CLOSE_WAIT on both proxy and runtime nodes.
- Envoy access and error logs show repeated "stream reset: PROTOCOL_ERROR" and traces indicating half-closed streams.
- Runtime logs: "no available worker" thread-pool warnings and intermittent "allocation failed" before some pods restarted gracefully.
- No runtime code deploys in prior 24 hours; small envoy healthcheck config tweak 6 hours earlier does not align with start time.

Investigation summary:
- Working hypothesis: a client-side pattern of TLS session reuse combined with ALPN negotiation fallback to HTTP/1.1 exposed a corner-case in the edge proxy where the previous TLS session could be left half-open. These half-open sockets accumulated in the proxy accept backlog, causing head-of-line blocking. Upstream connect attempts either timed out or failed, producing 5xx responses and backpressure on runtime worker threads which eventually led to allocation pressure on large-model pods.
- We reproduced the behavior in staging by simulating the TLS reuse + HTTP/1.1 fallback: accept queue growth and PROTOCOL_ERROR resets were observed on envoy.

Mitigations applied:
- Increased envoy worker threads and raised net.core.somaxconn on affected hosts at 18:32 UTC to relieve accept backlog (accept_queue_depth reduced from ~320 to ~40 within minutes).
- Deployed a temporary aggressive idle-close policy for streaming routes (idle-close 30s) at 18:40 UTC to avoid long-lived half-open sockets.
- Scaled ClaraDocs dedicated serving-runtime pool +30% at 18:45 UTC to give headroom while backlog drained.

Current status:
- Error rate returned to baseline by ~19:00 UTC. Customer confirmed most clients recovered; ClaraDocs noted a small number of dropped streaming messages but no persisted data loss.

Next steps / Action items:
1) Edge-proxy code fix: defensive ALPN downgrade handling to fully teardown previous TLS state on protocol fallback (PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1623).
2) Add alerting for accept_queue_depth > 200 with automated traffic rebalancing to spare hosts.
3) Re-evaluate and tighten keepalive/idle defaults for streaming clusters globally.
4) Execute chaos tests in staging simulating TLS reuse + protocol fallback to validate patch.
5) Customer outreach: recommend client SDK upgrade and share mitigation details.

Provisional root cause:
Edge-proxy did not fully handle ALPN/protocol downgrade in a small percentage of TLS session reuse cases, leaving sockets in a half-open state. The resulting accept backlog produced upstream connection failures and runtime overload under a concentrated short-stream burst pattern.
